paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Elijah had just seen God send fire on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:38), and one threat from Jezebel had him running for his life (1 Kings 19:3). Then he sat under a broom tree and said, "I have had enough, LORD" (1 Kings 19:4). If the man who saw that fire can hit a wall, you and I can too, and the passage never scolds him for it.

Look at what God does first. He doesn't give a speech. He sends bread and water, and an angel who says, "Get up and eat, or the journey will be too much for you" (1 Kings 19:5-7). Later God comes to Elijah not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire, but in "a still, small voice" (1 Kings 19:12). I think that tells us God meets a tired person gently, and sometimes the most helpful thing is a nap and a snack. I know a thing or two about being tired, and I'm LOUD about it.

Elijah said, "I am the only one left" (1 Kings 19:10, 14), and God answered, "I have reserved seven thousand in Israel" (1 Kings 19:18). Elijah felt alone, but he wasn't. Then God gave him real work to do, including a new prophet, Elisha, to come alongside him (1 Kings 19:16). So when you feel worn out and alone, baker, be honest with God like Elijah was, eat the bread He puts by your head, and get ready to hear what He says next. The story isn't over, and neither is the one God is writing in you.
